free_tier.stated: Starter plan, $0/month + usage: "per month + $5 in free credits"; "Free credits then usage-based pricing." The $5 is offered to new users and "in most cases your credits do not expire".
free_tier.notes: metered on spend: the USD 5 credit is spent against usage billed on four meters, USD 2.50 per GiB written, USD 0.33 per GiB per month stored, USD 0.0075 per TiB queried and USD 0.09 per GiB returned

per_object_cap.stated: 16,384 bytes per document, a Chroma Cloud quota; the total allowance is the credit

interface_detail: a REST API; Python and JS clients; the open-source server is self-hostable
chaining: the hosted Starter plan is a USD 5 credit for new accounts with usage-based billing after it; the open-source core, which the user installs and runs on a rented or free machine, is the last resort

limits.value: USD 5 of credits, which is a spend cap and not a tier

identity_cost.detail: sign-in with a GitHub or Google account; the sign-up page shows no card field; a vendor video posted 2025-06-30 says the USD 5 of free credits needs no credit card and says to add a credit card to keep using the service after the trial; the pricing FAQ lists credit card as the payment method for Starter and Team

reliability_note: a usage limit, whether set by the customer or by Chroma, pauses the service until the limit is changed

binding_note: the one-time USD 5 credit runs out first: it is counted per account across all collections, and at USD 2.50 per GiB written it pays for 2 GiB of writes before any storage, query or returned-data charge
